automation_name: AI Dev Wiki Leaf Update Watch

cutoff_window.rule: Only include public sources with visible publication or update dates within the last 7 days relative to the run timestamp. Exclude missing, ambiguous, future-dated, or boundary-only dates.

selection_method: New or previously unchecked leaves first, then oldest last_checked_at, ties by stable relative path sort. Excluded hubs, indexes, digests, federation, schema, glossary, known-defects, open-decisions, maintenance-log, topic-index, and dated source-synthesis pages.

federation_boundary.local_scope: AI-assisted development practice, workflow, governance, verification, implementation, and adoption implications

qualifying_updates.title: Infrastructure-level governance controls for production coding agents
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: TechRadar Pro published a Coder-authored perspective arguing that production coding-agent adoption is blocked less by model capability than by governance gaps. It recommends isolate, scope, and approve: ephemeral workspaces, narrow network and tool allowlists, scoped identities, real-time monitoring, human approval gates, and audit trails mapped to authenticated users.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Selected leaves already separate approval, ownership, governance, and verification responsibilities. This source gives fresh public support for treating isolation, scoped permissions, and approval as infrastructure controls rather than per-application prompt rules.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Ingest should consider reinforcing production-agent gates as enforceable harness and infrastructure policy: isolated execution, explicit network/tool scope, authenticated identity, anomaly monitoring, and human approval for ship-impacting actions.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Keep product and MCP background upstream; use this locally only as practice evidence for governance and approval leaves.

qualifying_updates.title: Agent governance must become a current permissions inventory
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: TechRadar Pro published a Zapier-authored governance perspective that frames older AI policies as insufficient for autonomous agents. It asks whether employees can see what AI tools can access, whether access can be revoked quickly, whether policies define permitted actions, and whether system-level agent access is governed.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: The selected adoption and governance leaves describe ownership rosters, operating agreements, and approval boundaries. This source adds a current public framing for permissions inventories, revocation paths, permitted-use definitions, and scoped agent identities.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Ingest should consider adding that ownership rosters should be discoverable permission inventories with revocation paths and affirmative allowed-use definitions, not only responsibility lists.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Route general MCP product context upstream; keep the local implication on operating controls.

qualifying_updates.title: Centralized governance layer positioned as response to agent sprawl
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: TechRadar Pro published an OutSystems-authored perspective arguing that rapid enterprise agent growth creates AI sprawl when teams apply fragmented human-in-the-loop rules and siloed standards. It recommends a centralized, neutral governance layer with visibility into running agents, connections, dependencies, standards, and shared knowledge.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Selected leaves cover operating agreements, governance controls, and process autonomy. This source supports the local balance between team autonomy and central governance: teams can choose workflows, but shared rules, visibility, and dependency knowledge need a common control plane.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Ingest should consider clarifying that decentralized agentic pods still need centralized discovery, standards, and governance telemetry to avoid local-rule drift.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Use as operating-model evidence; avoid duplicating broad vendor or analyst background.

qualifying_updates.title: Recent governance incident summary highlights agent identity, log integrity, and supply-chain gaps
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: AI Governance Institute summarized a Cloud Security Alliance incident report as evidence of governance gaps in agent deployments, highlighting prompt injection, poisoned agent registries, unauthorized resource use, inter-agent cascade risk, weak identity binding, incomplete audit trails, and missing shadow-traffic detection.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Selected governance, approval, ownership, and durable-skill leaves all depend on the claim that agent autonomy needs enforceable identity, audit, and supply-chain controls. This source gives a current summary that ties those controls to concrete incident classes.

qualifying_updates.title: Mandiant frames AI-assisted security workflows around guardrails and structural integrity
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Google Cloud Mandiant published guidance for AI-assisted vulnerability management, saying security teams can accelerate work with AI while preserving structural integrity through operational guardrails and scenario-based workflows.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Lifecycle review gates and verification-tax leaves need examples where AI acceleration does not remove security process obligations. This source supports a security-specific local pattern: AI can assist vulnerability workflows only when guardrails and scenario boundaries are part of the workflow design.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Ingest should consider connecting AI-assisted security repair gates to scenario-level guardrails and structural integrity checks rather than generic acceleration claims.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Keep vendor/service background upstream; local page should capture the security-workflow gate implication.

qualifying_updates.title: Gemini Enterprise demos package build, evaluate, deploy, and monitor skills for coding agents
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Google Cloud published Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform demos and described an Agents CLI that can be installed into coding agents such as Antigravity, Claude Code, and Codex, giving them skills for ADK and Agent Platform so they can scaffold, evaluate, deploy, and monitor agents from an editor. One demo covers an event-driven approval agent with human-in-the-loop handling.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Selected leaves on durable instructions, portable skills, tier conventions, approval boundaries, and verification loops all track how reusable agent capabilities become operational practice. This source shows a current vendor packaging pattern: skills/runbooks are becoming the delivery mechanism for build-evaluate-deploy-monitor workflows.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Ingest should consider describing portable skills as operational packages that include evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and approval workflow knowledge, not just prompt snippets.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Route product details upstream; keep only downstream practice consequences for skills and approval leaves.

qualifying_updates.title: LangChain publishes microVM sandbox guidance for agent execution
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: LangChain published guidance arguing that agents executing code need isolated, disposable work environments with their own filesystem, shell, package manager, network boundary, credentials proxy, resource limits, lifecycle controls, observability, and sandbox output treated as untrusted data.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Selected governance, verification, approval, and adoption leaves already emphasize controlled autonomy. This source gives a concrete current architecture for agent workspaces and the non-agentic-read pattern at sandbox boundaries.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Ingest should consider strengthening sandbox guidance around hardware virtualization, credential injection outside the runtime, per-task resource ceilings, execution observability, and treating sandbox outputs as untrusted inputs.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Product specifics belong upstream; local implication belongs in governance and verification practice leaves.

qualifying_updates.title: AgentCompass proposes unified, trajectory-aware agent evaluation infrastructure
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: The arXiv preprint AgentCompass introduces an open-source evaluation infrastructure that separates benchmark, harness, and environment components, supports fault-tolerant asynchronous execution, and records trajectory-level analysis across tool use, web research, scientific reasoning, agentic coding, and productivity benchmarks.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Selected evaluation leaves emphasize trajectory-level assessment and repeatable verification loops. AgentCompass supports the local practice of evaluating heterogeneous agent harnesses with comparable logging and provenance rather than relying on final-answer scores.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Ingest should consider adding benchmark-harness-environment separation and trajectory provenance as evaluation design criteria for local agent workflows.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Route broad benchmark/entity profiles upstream; keep the local implication on evaluation infrastructure shape.

qualifying_updates.title: Current agent evaluation guides converge on outcomes, traces, tools, cost, and safety
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: Aasher Kamal published a guide stating that production agent evaluation should test environment outcomes, tool-call trajectories, permissions, recovery, and cost rather than only final prose. It recommends observable job definitions and evaluating whether state actually changed correctly.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: This directly reinforces selected trajectory evaluation, verification loop, and acceptance-gate pages: an agent is done only when the environment outcome and path evidence support the completion claim.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Ingest should consider making outcome-state validation explicit in acceptance gates, especially for agents that mutate files, records, tickets, calendars, or deployment state.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Use as current practice evidence; verify against stronger primary eval sources during ingest where possible.

qualifying_updates.title: Production agent-eval guidance emphasizes online traces and security gates
qualifying_updates.factual_summary: TECHSY published a production agent-evaluation guide describing a three-layer system for live traces: score the whole trajectory, validate right-tool/right-argument/right-step behavior, run offline and online metrics continuously, and gate on security vulnerabilities such as jailbreak, PII, and tool misuse.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters_for_leaf: Selected verification and governance leaves need the connection between evaluation telemetry and release gates. This source supports treating security and tool-use checks as release criteria, not optional observability.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Ingest should consider linking online trace evaluation, tool-call correctness, and security gates into the acceptance-gate model for production agents.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Keep vendor/platform selection upstream; local page should capture continuous evaluation and security-gate practice.
